name: com.garphield/garphield
title: Garphield
description: Build, style, lay out, share and export network graphs from tables and graph files.

tools.name: garphield_create
tools.description: Create a stored graph document from data and return its reference (doc). Pass exactly one of: graph (node-link JSON: nodes [{id, ...attributes}] and edges [{source, target, ...attributes}]), table (CSV text for links, optionally nodes), file (a GEXF, GraphML, GML, node-link JSON, Cytoscape JSON, edge list, Matrix Market, graph6 or .gph text), or url. url fetches from three public sources only, and refuses every other site: a file on GitHub (raw.githubusercontent.com, a github.com/<owner>/<repo>/blob/... page, or a gist's raw link), a Google Sheet shared with anyone with the link or published to the web, or a table on a Wikipedia article (<lang>.wikipedia.org/wiki/<Title>; url.wikitable picks which). For a table, name the link columns with url.source and url.target. The result lists the bindable fields with their ids and types, the names a binding accepts.

name.description: Title shown in the workbench and in share previews.

items.description: A node: its id plus any attributes (label, role, x, y, ...).
A link between two node ids, plus any attributes (weight, ...).

links.description: NetworkX's older name for edges; pass one or the other.

items.description: A link between two node ids, plus any attributes (weight, ...).

graph.description: Node-link JSON. Nodes named only by a link are created. Ids are stored as strings.

edges.description: Links table: CSV, TSV or semicolon text with a header row.

nodes.description: Optional node table with a header row; its rows add attributes.

source.description: Links column holding the source id. Default "source".

target.description: Links column holding the target id. Default "target".

nodeId.description: Node table column holding the id. Default "id".

table.description: Tables as text. Columns match case-insensitively; numeric cells become numbers and blank cells stay missing.

file.description: A graph file in a format the workbench opens (not DOT).

href.description: An https link to a GitHub file (raw.githubusercontent.com, github.com/<owner>/<repo>/blob/..., gist.githubusercontent.com), a Google Sheet shared publicly or published (docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/...; #gid= picks the tab), or a Wikipedia article (<lang>.wikipedia.org/wiki/<Title>). Other sites are refused.

source.description: For a table (CSV/TSV file, sheet, Wikipedia table): the column holding the source id. Default "source".

target.description: For a table: the column holding the target id. Default "target".

wikitable.description: Wikipedia only: which wikitable on the page, counting from 1 in page order. Default 1.

url.description: Data fetched from a public link. A table's columns match case-insensitively; when source or target is missing, the error lists the columns.

tools.name: garphield_inspect
tools.description: Describe a stored graph: size, density, connected components, whether it has saved positions, its data fields (ids to bind, type num or cat, missing counts, ranges or example values), the channels and the types each accepts, the computed algorithms, the current view config (bindings, filters and saved sets), and a quality grade of the saved layout. The field ids it lists are the names a binding accepts.

doc.description: Document reference: a stored document id, a file path, or "current" in the workbench.

include.description: Sections to return. Default ["fields", "channels", "config"]. "algorithms" lists computed sources (degree, louvain, ...) with their params; "scales" gives what each binding draws (every value's mark, label and count, or the numeric domain and range), in the form a binding's scale takes; "quality" grades the saved positions.

tools.name: garphield_style
tools.description: Bind data fields or computed algorithms to visual channels, and set the layout mode, how links show direction (arrows), theme, tooltip templates for nodes and links, drawing values (appearance: link width and opacity, node size, curvature, label placement) and structure (Group by rings, the Backbone, or a merge into one node per field value) of a stored graph. Example binding: {"channel": "edgeWidth", "field": "amount_bn"}; a bare field name resolves to the field on the channel's target (node or edge). Strict and atomic: if any entry is invalid nothing is written and each problem comes back with a path, the expected values and suggestions. Merges by channel unless replace is true. The result echoes every stored binding. preview: true also returns a small image of the styled graph; it adds a render (10-20 s on the hosted server), so ask for it when you mean to look.

doc.description: Document reference: a stored document id, a file path, or "current" in the workbench.

channel.description: Channel id, e.g. color, size, edgeWidth, edgeColor, hull.

field.description: A data field by name ("amount_bn") or id ("efield:amount_bn"); a bare name resolves to the field on the channel's target.

algorithm.description: A computed source id, e.g. degree, pagerank, louvain.

set.description: A set id saved in the document.

params.description: Algorithm params; each must be declared and in range.

source.description: The stored wire form instead of field/algorithm/set; requires resultType.

resultType.description: Override the source's type, e.g. cat to colour a numeric field by value. Required with source.

value.description: A data value, matched by its text form: 3 and "3" are the same value. A set binding's values are true (member) and false.

mark.description: The mark for this value: a CSS colour (#rrggbb, rgb(), hsl()) for color, edgeColor, border, hull and contour; circle, square, triangle or diamond for shape; solid or dashed for edgeStyle; a glyph (text, inline <svg>, or image URL) for glyph.

label.description: What the legend shows for this value, instead of the value.

categories.description: One entry per value, in legend order. Values not listed keep the default palette or shape cycle.

mark.description: The mark for this value: a CSS colour (#rrggbb, rgb(), hsl()) for color, edgeColor, border, hull and contour; circle, square, triangle or diamond for shape; solid or dashed for edgeStyle; a glyph (text, inline <svg>, or image URL) for glyph.

label.description: What the legend shows for this value, instead of the value.

missing.description: The mark and label for items with no value.

anyOf.description: Marks and labels for a cat or set binding's values.

domain.description: The data values that map to the two ends of the range. Values outside it are clamped.

range.description: Two lengths in px (size: node radius; edgeWidth: link width), or two or more CSS colours as ramp stops (color, edgeColor).

anyOf.description: A pinned domain and range for a num binding.

scale.description: Explicit marks for the binding's values. Omit it to use the defaults.

remove.description: Unbind this channel. Pass only channel with it.

items.description: One binding: a channel plus exactly one of field, algorithm, set or source; or a channel with remove.

replace.description: true replaces every binding with this list; false (default) merges by channel.

layout.description: Layout the workbench uses on open. Sets config only and computes no positions.

edgeDirection.description: How links show their direction in a directed graph: arrow (arrowheads), tapered (each link narrows toward its target, the workbench default), flow (animated) or line (none).

theme.description: Default theme for embed links (and the saved view, if the document has one). null clears it; a saved view returns to the light default.

tooltipTemplate.description: Embed tooltip Markdown with {attribute} placeholders, e.g. "### {label}\n{role}". null clears it.

linkTooltipTemplate.description: Embed hover card for links: the same Markdown over link attributes, plus {source} and {target} (the end nodes' labels), e.g. "### {source} to {target}\n{tasks} tasks". A line that is only {@markdown field} renders that attribute's own lists and emphasis. Without it links get no card; null clears it.

groups.description: Group by: nodes drawn as dots in nested rings, one ring per value. null turns it off.

id.description: A categorical node algorithm: louvain, leiden, label_propagation, asyn_lpa, greedy_modularity, k_clique, spectral_bisection, kernighan_lin, connected_components.

anyOf.description: An algorithm's groups, written as a binding source: connected_components draws one ring per connected component, with isolated nodes in one ring.

by.description: Levels, outer to inner, each once: node fields and algorithms, e.g. [{"kind": "algorithm", "id": "connected_components"}, "team"]; [] groups by nested Louvain communities.

links.description: Links drawn besides those at hovered or selected nodes: none (default), inside (within the innermost group) or all (faded).

backbone.description: Backbone: only the links that carry the structure. The workbench draws it where it can build one for the graph. null turns it off.

background.description: How links outside the Backbone draw: auto (default), faded or hidden.

merge.description: Merge: one node per value of the fields, with the links between two merged nodes combined into one per direction. null turns it off.

by.description: Node fields; one merged node per value, each field once.

label.description: Label template over the merged fields: {field}, {members} (how many nodes merged), and {field by other} (field per value of other, joined " → "), e.g. "{role}  {tasks by side}".

combine.description: Rules per node or link field. Defaults: numbers sum, the size channel's field adds areas, categories keep the most common value, long text is listed.

structure.description: How the workbench and embeds draw the graph on open: Group by, Backbone and merge. Each part changes only what is given. A merge draws with neither groups nor the Backbone: turning it on turns them off, and turning either on turns it off. The network and its positions are unchanged.

appearance.description: The Style pane's drawing values, e.g. {"linkWidth": 4, "linkOpacity": 0.7}. Merges with the values already set; null returns them all to the defaults.

nodeSize.description: Multiplies every node's drawn size. 0.5 to 2.5; default 1.

nodeGap.description: Pixels kept clear between nodes. 0 to 8; default 2.

labelBudget.description: Label density: how many node labels show at once. 0.5 to 10; default 1.

labelPlacement.description: Node labels beside the node (default) or centred on it.

linkWidth.description: Multiplies every link's drawn width. 0.1 to 8; default 1.

linkOutline.description: Link outline width in pixels. 0 to 20; default 2.

arrowSize.description: Arrowhead size, for flow links. 0.5 to 3; default 2.

curvature.description: How far links bend, from 0 (straight) to 100. 0 to 100; default 0.

linkOpacity.description: Multiplies link opacity; under 1 is fainter. 0.05 to 2; default 1.

preview.description: true returns a 600x400 image of the saved graph, so you can check it for overlapping nodes, tangles and unreadable labels and fix them. A render can take 10-20 s and counts toward the host's image limit; the change is saved even when no preview can be made. Default false.

tools.name: garphield_focus
tools.description: Save named sets of nodes and focus the view on them; the app, share links, embeds and PNG exports all show the result. A set comes from exactly one of: nodes (ids), edges ([source, target] pairs, kept as their endpoints), path (a shortest path from one node to another), top (the k highest or lowest by a field or algorithm such as degree), or match (a range, values, or one node's value of a field or algorithm, e.g. a louvain community). filters fade (default) or hide everything outside a set ({"set": "path"}) or outside a range or values of a field or algorithm. mark rings a set's nodes. clear empties the filters, or with "all" every set too. Example, highlight a path: {"sets": [{"id": "route", "path": {"from": "a", "to": "e"}}], "filters": [{"set": "route"}]}. Show only the top 20 by degree: {"sets": [{"id": "hubs", "top": {"algorithm": "degree", "k": 20}}], "filters": [{"set": "hubs", "mode": "hide"}]}. Strict and atomic: if anything is invalid nothing is written, and each problem comes back with a path and suggestions (unknown node ids suggest near ids and nodes with that label).

doc.description: Document reference: a stored document id, a file path, or "current" in the workbench.

clear.description: Applied first. "filters" empties the filter stack; "all" also deletes every set and every binding that reads one.

id.description: The set's id (letters, digits, _ . : -). An existing id is replaced.

edges.description: The endpoints of these links, each a [source, target] pair of node ids.

path.description: The nodes on a shortest path, following link direction on a directed graph.

top.description: The k nodes (or the endpoints of the k links, for an edge source) with the highest or lowest values.

field.description: A data field by name ("role") or id ("field:role", "efield:amount_bn"); a bare name resolves to the node field first.

algorithm.description: A computed source id, e.g. degree, pagerank, betweenness, louvain.

params.description: Algorithm params; each must be declared and in range.

match.description: The nodes whose value meets one criterion: a range, values, or the value of a node.

field.description: A data field by name ("role") or id ("field:role", "efield:amount_bn"); a bare name resolves to the node field first.

algorithm.description: A computed source id, e.g. degree, pagerank, betweenness, louvain.

params.description: Algorithm params; each must be declared and in range.

range.description: Numeric sources: keep values from min to max inclusive. An omitted bound is the source's own minimum or maximum.

values.description: Categorical sources (or a numeric field read as categories): keep these values. Community ids are numbers from 0.

node.description: Keep the value this node has, e.g. {"algorithm": "louvain", "node": "valjean"} for that node's community.

remove.description: Delete the set. Pass only id with it.

items.description: Create or replace a named set from exactly one of nodes, edges, path, top or match; or remove one.

filters.description: Merged into the filter stack by id.

id.description: Filter entry id. Default "focus-<set id>" or "focus-<source id>"; an existing id is replaced.

set.description: Keep the members of this set (saved or defined in this call).

field.description: A data field by name ("role") or id ("field:role", "efield:amount_bn"); a bare name resolves to the node field first.

algorithm.description: A computed source id, e.g. degree, pagerank, betweenness, louvain.

params.description: Algorithm params; each must be declared and in range.

range.description: Numeric sources: keep values from min to max inclusive. An omitted bound is the source's own minimum or maximum.

values.description: Categorical sources (or a numeric field read as categories): keep these values. Community ids are numbers from 0.

node.description: Keep the value this node has, e.g. {"algorithm": "louvain", "node": "valjean"} for that node's community.

mode.description: fade (default) dims what the filter drops; hide removes it from the drawing.

remove.description: Delete the filter entry with this id. Pass only id with it.

items.description: Keep a set, or keep what one criterion on a field or algorithm selects; fade or hide the rest.

mark.description: Ring this set's nodes (the border channel bound to the set). null removes a set ring.

tools.name: garphield_layout
tools.description: Compute and save node positions for a stored graph with the workbench's own layout recipes, and grade the result with its quality gate. Optional: a graph without positions is laid out by the browser when it opens. Use this to bake positions (for a gallery file or a stable share) or to get a quality grade. Reports which engine ran. Large graphs over the host's budget return LAYOUT_TOO_LARGE; clear: true removes saved positions. preview: true also returns a small image of the result, to check for overlaps, tangles and unreadable labels against the grade's findings; it adds a render (10-20 s on the hosted server), so ask for it when you mean to look.

doc.description: Document reference: a stored document id, a file path, or "current" in the workbench.

mode.description: force (production Blend, or ForceAtlas2 for large graphs), levels (layered), or geo (the browser places nodes by their coordinate fields). Default: the document's layout, else force.

aspect.description: Width over height of the frame to fit. Default 1.6.

roots.description: Node ids for the top level.

levelAttribute.description: A numeric node field that orders the levels.

clear.description: Remove saved positions instead, so the browser lays the graph out when it opens. Pass only doc with it.

preview.description: true returns a 600x400 image of the saved graph, so you can check it for overlapping nodes, tangles and unreadable labels and fix them. A render can take 10-20 s and counts toward the host's image limit; the change is saved even when no preview can be made. Default false.

tools.name: garphield_validate
tools.description: Check a stored document (doc) or a raw .gph document (document) the way the workbench would load it, strictly: the schema, the graph, every binding against the graph's fields and the channel rules, and the filter stack. Returns ok, errors (code, path, message, expected, suggestions) and warnings such as UNLAID (no saved positions).

doc.description: Document reference: a stored document id, a file path, or "current" in the workbench.

document.description: A whole .gph document as JSON, for callers who wrote one themselves.

tools.name: garphield_share
tools.description: Get links that open a stored graph in the Garphield workbench and in its embeddable view, plus an iframe snippet. Depending on the host the link points at the stored document (anyone with the link can open it, until expiresAt), carries the whole document in the URL (selfContained), or, in the workbench, carries just the view of a built-in sample or generator. Rendering happens in the viewer's browser; a graph without saved positions is laid out when it opens.

doc.description: Document reference: a stored document id, a file path, or "current" in the workbench.

target.description: Which link `url` is: the full workbench ("app", default) or the chromeless embed.

chrome.description: Embed controls to show. Omitted: the embed's defaults. -wordmark takes the link off the Garphield wordmark; the mark stays.

theme.description: Embed theme. Default: the document's theme, if it has one.

tools.name: garphield_export
tools.description: Export a stored graph as a .gph project (with its view config and positions), as node-link JSON, GEXF, GraphML or GML, or as a PNG where the host can render. Text formats come back inline up to the host's result limit; gph also reports where the stored file is, when the host has a location. The export is a frozen copy: later style or layout calls do not change it. Where the host stores images, a png export is also kept as the document's preview image.

doc.description: Document reference: a stored document id, a file path, or "current" in the workbench.

format.description: gph is the full Garphield project; nodeLink, gexf, graphml and gml carry the graph and its attributes; png is an image where the host can render one.

inline.description: gph only: false returns just the stored location and size, without the text. Default true.
